checks: For every odd positive multiple N of 3, all stated destinations lie in the finite state set; the exceptional grid index (-N+3)/2 is integral.
The transition barycenters are exactly (L+2R)/3 with L<R, hence use only the permitted one-sided hypothesis.

Repeated right moves strictly increase each nonabsorbing state and force absorption in a uniformly bounded number of moves for that fixed N. Iterating a positive absorption probability proves almost-sure absorption.

On each fixed finite state space both the numerical states and all real-valued g values are bounded. Bounded convergence therefore justifies terminal numerical expectation and the terminal g inequality without continuity or optional stopping gaps.
Positive-to-negative crossing occurs only from 1/N to -1/N. All later negative transitions remain nonpositive, including the exceptional transition since N>=3.
Starting at -1/N, terminal mean -1/N gives 2q2+3q3=1/N. By the first-entry Markov property, original negative terminal mass is at most 1/(2N).

Only four fixed finite terminal g values appear as N tends to infinity. Vanishing negative mass and preserved mean give p1->1/3, p0->2/3, proving g(1/3)<=(2g(0)+g(1))/3 without any regularity assumption.
The increasing affine transformation for u>v yields precisely the reversed-order inequality alleged to fail. Thus no such function exists.
